Test Description: Validates reset values and read/write behavior of gp0_gpio_8 through gp0_gpio_30. For each register, the test skips entries flagged as non-testable, verifies readable reset values with bit 0 ignored, writes a series of data patterns masked by the write mask, and confirms read-back values match the expected combination of written bits and preserved default bits for non-writable fields. The test reports pass only if all applicable checks succeed.
Meta Test Description:
The testcase executes test_case(), which performs two phases: (1) default/reset value verification via chk_rst_val(), and (2) write/read verification via chk_rd_wr().

In chk_rst_val(): for i=0..CNT-1, addr = addr_array[i]. If skip_rst_array[i] == 1, the entry is skipped. If read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000, the entry is treated as not readable and skipped. Otherwise, data_rd = read_reg(addr), data = (data_rd & 0xfffffffe), and data is compared to default_value_array[i]. On mismatch, def_fail_cnt is incremented and a failure message is printed; otherwise a pass message is optionally printed when DEBUG_DISPLAY is enabled.

In chk_rd_wr(): the code iterates over six write patterns chk_val[6] = {0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0xf5f5f5f5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}. For each pattern j and for each i=0..CNT-1, addr = addr_array[i]. If skip_array[i] == 1, the address is skipped. If write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000, the address is considered not writable and is skipped for writing. Otherwise, write_reg(addr, (data_wr & write_mask_array[i])) is performed. Then in the read-back loop, for each i, if skip_array[i] == 1, continue; if write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000, continue; if read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000, continue; else data_rd = (read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]). The expected value is computed as: wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff); exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])). If data_rd != exp_val, wr_fail_cnt is incremented and a failure message is printed; otherwise a pass message is optionally printed when DEBUG_DISPLAY is enabled.

After both phases, test_case() calls finish(1) if (def_fail_cnt > 0 || wr_fail_cnt > 0), otherwise finish(0). A soft_reset_chk() helper exists but is compiled out (#ifdef 0); it references SOFT_RST_REG_ADDRESS and SOFT_RST_REG_DATA.
Remarks: Requires platform support for read_reg, write_reg, and finish functions. Registers marked in the skip lists are intentionally not exercised. Reset-value comparison ignores bit 0 of the read value. The optional soft reset sequence is disabled in this build.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. For each of the registers gp0_gpio_8 through gp0_gpio_30: if the register is not marked as skipped and is readable, read the register and verify its reset value matches the expected value with bit 0 ignored.
2. For each of six predefined data patterns, and for each register gp0_gpio_8 through gp0_gpio_30: if the register is not marked as skipped and is writable and readable, write the pattern masked by the write mask, then read back and verify the masked value equals the expected combination of written bits and preserved default bits for non-writable fields.
3. Declare PASS only if all applicable reset checks and write/read checks pass across all patterns and registers; otherwise declare FAIL.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry: test_case()
1) Call chk_rst_val():
   - Loop i = 0..CNT-1:
     a) addr = addr_array[i]
     b) If (skip_rst_array[i] == 1) continue
     c) If (read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue
     d) data_rd = read_reg(addr)
     e) data = (data_rd & 0xfffffffe)
     f) If (data == default_value_array[i]) -> PASS; else def_fail_cnt++ and print failure details
2) Call chk_rd_wr():
   - Define patterns chk_val[6] = {0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0xf5f5f5f5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}
   - For each j = 0..5:
     a) data_wr = chk_val[j]
     b) Write phase loop i = 0..CNT-1: write_reg(addr, (data_wr & write_mask_array[i]))
     c) Read/verify phase loop i = 0..CNT-1: data_rd = (read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]); exp_val computed; compare
3) Completion: If (def_fail_cnt > 0 || wr_fail_cnt > 0) finish(1); else finish(0)

Test Description: Validates level-based interrupt generation and clearing for GP0 GPIO pins 8 through 39. The test configures each pin for input mode with level-triggered interrupts, enables the group interrupt via gp0_intr1_intr_en1, stimulates the corresponding pin state via a memory-backed pattern, and waits for the interrupt handler to run. It then verifies that the per-pin raw status is set, the group status reflects the active pin, and that both per-pin and group status clear correctly when commanded.
Meta Test Description: The testcase initializes error tracking and conditionally enables the appropriate platform interrupt line. It programs the system-level interrupt enable for the selected GPIO instance. For i = 0..31 (GPIO8..GPIO39), it configures each per-pin register at an address stride from the base (gp0_gpio_8 + i*4) with 0x00180000 (input mode with level interrupt), waits, enables the corresponding group interrupt bit by writing (1<<i) to gp0_intr1_intr_en1, waits briefly, writes 0xFFFFFFFF to a memory location (0xA0243ffc) to stimulate activity, sets a pending flag, and spins until the interrupt handler clears the pending flag. After a delay, a second pass programs each pin for the opposite level selection by writing 0x00100000 to the same per-pin address, enables the group bit, writes the complement pattern ~(1<<i) to 0xA0243ffc, sets the pending flag, and again waits until the handler completes. The interrupt handler reads the per-pin register for the active index and checks the raw status bit (bit 1). If set, it reads gp0_intr1_intr_sts1 to confirm the corresponding group bit is set. It then clears the per-pin interrupt by writing 0x00110000 to the per-pin register, waits, and verifies the readback equals 0x100001. It disables the group interrupt by writing 0x00000000 to gp0_intr1_intr_en1 and verifies gp0_intr1_intr_sts1 clears to zero. Finally, it writes to the system RAW_STCR register to clear the system-level interrupt bit and verifies that the bit is cleared by a subsequent read. If any expected condition fails at any step, the error counter is incremented. The test exits via finish(test_err), reporting success when test_err == 0.
Remarks: Requires platform interrupt routing and an installed interrupt handler to clear the pending flag. Group interrupt enable and status registers must be accessible. The test relies on a memory-backed stimulus location to drive pin-level conditions. Ensure system-level interrupt enable is configured for the selected GPIO instance before running.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Configure the system to route the GPIO interrupt for the active instance and enable it.
2. For each GPIO pin from 8 to 39, program the corresponding GP0 GPIO per-pin register range (starting at gp0_gpio_8) for input mode with level-high interrupt selection.
3. For each configured pin, enable the corresponding bit in gp0_intr1_intr_en1.
4. Apply a stimulus pattern that asserts the selected pin level and wait for the interrupt to be serviced.
5. In the interrupt service phase, verify that the per-pin raw status is asserted and that gp0_intr1_intr_sts1 reports the correct group bit for the active pin. Clear the per-pin interrupt, verify the per-pin readback shows the cleared state, disable gp0_intr1_intr_en1, and verify gp0_intr1_intr_sts1 clears to zero.
6. Repeat steps 2-5 with level-low selection for each GPIO pin by reprogramming the per-pin configuration and applying the complementary stimulus pattern.
7. Declare PASS if all pins generate the expected interrupts in both level configurations and all clear operations succeed without errors; otherwise declare FAIL.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry: test_case()
1) Init: test_err = 0; conditionally enable platform interrupt: if GPIO0 then GIC_EnableIRQ(87); if GPIO1 then GIC_EnableIRQ(88).
2) System-level interrupt enable: if GPIO0 then write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR).
3) Level-high loop (i = 0..31): write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4), 0x00180000); write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, wr_val); write_reg(0xA0243ffc, 0xFFFFFFFF); wait for ISR.
4) Level-low loop (i = 0..31): write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4), 0x00100000); similar sequence.
5) ISR: verify raw status, group status, clear per-pin, clear group, clear system.
6) Exit: finish(test_err).
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: PASS: For each GPIO pin 8-39 in both level-high and level-low configurations, an interrupt is generated, the group status reflects the active pin, per-pin and group status clear correctly, and the system-level interrupt status is cleared. FAIL: Any missing interrupt, incorrect group status, failed per-pin clear readback, failed group status clear, or uncleared system-level status.
Meta Validation / Acceptance Criteria: During Default_IRQHandler(): require (read per-pin) (rdata & 0x2) != 0x0 to confirm raw status. Require (read gp0_intr1_intr_sts1) (rdata_grp & (1<<i)) != 0 for the active pin. After clearing per-pin by write 0x00110000, require subsequent read of per-pin register equals 0x100001. After disabling group by writing 0x00000000 to gp0_intr1_intr_en1, require gp0_intr1_intr_sts1 reads 0x0. For GPIO0 path: after write to MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 with LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR, require (readback & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR) == 0. Overall PASS when test_err == 0 at finish(); otherwise FAIL.
